section_summary.extract_value: This introductory section explores the complex relationship between intelligence and creativity, outlining five possible relationships proposed by Sternberg and O'Hara (1999). It discusses influential models of intelligence that treat creativity as a lower-order factor, such as Guilford's structure-of-intellect model (divergent production), Carrol's three-stratum model (retrieval ability), and the Berlin model of intelligence structure (imaginativeness). The section also introduces Guilford's "threshold hypothesis," which suggests a varying correlation between IQ and divergent production depending on the level of cognitive ability.
